links.comparator_used: Same medical LLMs fine-tuned only on public clinical datasets (I2B2/N2C2, emrQA) and applied to local Pakistani EHR data without local fine-tuning
links.outcome: Medical concept extraction (F1) and medical question answering (ROUGE-L, BLEU) on local EHR notes
links.effect: Without local fine-tuning, external validation on local data fell by at least 15% in F1 (MCE) and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU (MQA) versus internal validation. Local fine-tuning gave a 7.5% to 15% increase in F1 for MCE and a 27% to 53% increase in ROUGE-L and BLEU for MQA.
links.tradeoff: Local fine-tuning needs appropriate clinical and technical expertise and curated local data. The authors describe it as substantially less resource-intensive than training LLMs from scratch.
links.quote: However, fine-tuning the LLMs with local EHR data significantly improved model performance across both tasks, yielding a 7.5% to 15% increase in the F1 score for MCE and a 27% to 53% increase in ROUGE-L and BLEU scores for MQA.
